Class AIRequestLimiterTest

java.lang.Object
tests.AIRequestLimiterTest
class AIRequestLimiterTest extends Object

Title: AIRequestLimiterTest Class

Description: JUnit tests for the AIRequestLimiter prototype (HW3 Task 5). The tests are A1 to A11 from "TP3 Testing Details and Rationale.pdf", and together they cover Requirement 1 of "TP3 Testing Requirements.pdf": each user can make at most 20 AI requests in any 60-minute period, with a clear message when the limit is reached (CWE-770).

These tests were written before the AIRequestLimiter class (test-driven development). Each test passes the time in as a number instead of using the real clock, so the tests run instantly, give the same result every time, and can check exact boundaries like one second before the hour is up.

How to read the results: JUnit shows a green check for each test that passed. A test passes when the limiter returns exactly the expected text: "" means the request was allowed, and any other text is the message the user would see.

    • minute

      static long minute(int m)

      Method: long minute(int m)

      Description: Turns minutes after the start of the test into the millisecond time the limiter uses. This keeps the tests readable: minute(20) instead of 1200000.

      Parameters:
      m - is the number of minutes
      Returns:
      that many minutes in milliseconds

    • limiterWith20Used

      static limits.AIRequestLimiter limiterWith20Used(String user)

      Method: AIRequestLimiter limiterWith20Used(String user)

      Description: Makes a limiter where the user has made 20 requests, one each minute from minute 0 to minute 19. This is the setup for A2 to A7.

      Parameters:
      user - is the username making the requests
      Returns:
      the limiter, with the user at the limit

    • A1_firstRequestAllowed

      @Test void A1_firstRequestAllowed()

      Test: A1 (positive)

      Requirement: a user can make AI requests (normal use works).

      Input: Ron's first request at minute 0. Expected: "" and 19 requests left.

    • A2_twentiethRequestAllowed

      @Test void A2_twentiethRequestAllowed()

      Test: A2 (positive, boundary)

      Requirement: up to 20 requests in 60 minutes are allowed.

      Input: 20 requests from minute 0 to 19. Expected: the 20th returns "" and 0 are left.

    • A3_twentyFirstRequestRefused

      @Test void A3_twentyFirstRequestRefused()

      Test: A3 (negative, boundary)

      Requirement: the 21st request in 60 minutes is refused, and the message says how long to wait.

      Input: a 21st request at minute 20. Expected: refused, try again in 40 minutes, because the minute-0 request counts until minute 60.

    • A4_otherUserNotBlocked

      @Test void A4_otherUserNotBlocked()

      Test: A4 (positive)

      Requirement: each user has their own count.

      Input: Ron is at the limit, and Elijah makes his first request at minute 20. Expected: "" for Elijah.

    • A5_allowedAfterAnHour

      @Test void A5_allowedAfterAnHour()

      Test: A5 (positive, time boundary)

      Requirement: a request stops counting once it is 60 minutes old.

      Input: Ron at the limit tries again at exactly minute 60. Expected: "", because the minute-0 request is now exactly 60 minutes old.

    • A6_refusedOneSecondBeforeTheHour

      @Test void A6_refusedOneSecondBeforeTheHour()

      Test: A6 (negative, time boundary)

      Requirement: requests still count until the full 60 minutes have passed, and the wait is never shown as 0 minutes.

      Input: Ron at the limit tries at minute 59, second 59. Expected: refused, try again in 1 minute (1 second rounded up).

    • A7_refusedRequestsNotCounted

      @Test void A7_refusedRequestsNotCounted()

      Test: A7 (positive)

      Requirement: refused requests are not counted.

      Input: Ron at the limit is refused 5 times at minute 30, then tries at minute 60. Expected: "". If the refused tries were counted, he would still be blocked.

    • A8_emptyUserRefused

      @Test void A8_emptyUserRefused()

      Test: A8 (negative)

      Requirement: a user who isn't logged in can't make AI requests.

      Input: an empty username. Expected: the not-logged-in message, and 0 requests left.

    • A9_nullUserRefused

      @Test void A9_nullUserRefused()

      Test: A9 (negative)

      Requirement: a missing user must not crash the program.

      Input: a null username. Expected: the not-logged-in message and 0 requests left, with no NullPointerException.

    • A10_zeroLimitRefused

      @Test void A10_zeroLimitRefused()

      Test: A10 (negative)

      Requirement: the limit can't be set to 0 or less by mistake.

      Input: a limit of 0. Expected: IllegalArgumentException with the message "The AI request limit must be at least 1."

    • A11_limitOfOne

      @Test void A11_limitOfOne()

      Test: A11 (positive, boundary on the setting)

      Requirement: the smallest allowed limit, 1, works.

      Input: a limit of 1 and two requests at minute 0. Expected: the first returns "" and the second is refused.
